Title: Re-igniting Karachi

NewsContent:
"Enlighten us, but make it quick’ is the motto of Ignite events worldwide where geek presenters unfold their genius in five minutes using only 20 slides. Ignite Karachi II, the second in a series of events, organised by Critical Creative Innovative Thinking (CCIT) – a platform at AKU that promotes creativity and innovation in biomedicine and healthcare – presented 10 Igniters who spoke on a variety of topics ranging from grassroots entrepreneurship and pharmacy activism to the creative use of a degree and the ever-growing issue of elder abuse.

Rija Binte Rehan, a final year medical student at AKU led off the proceedings highlighting a unique connection between astronomy and medicine, inspiring the audience to think out of the box. She spoke about the need to indulge in diverse hobbies alongside studies and work which allowed one to look at a bigger scenario. This may be one way for healthcare professionals to adopt a more holistic approach in clinical practice.

Faraz Khan, a UK-based social entrepreneur from Pakistan and Viraj Mane, a scientist, inventor and entrepreneur were not physically present; however, their Ignites were well received. Standing in on behalf of Faraz Khan, Sadaf Mehmood gave an introduction to Potential Enterprise Mapping Strategy, an initiative that is helping improve the socio-economic status of impoverished communities. Mane linked careers with creativity and was of the opinion that unconventional ideas can truly change the way we look at the realms of health and medicine.

One such unconventional idea was presented by Faysal Subhani, a final year medical student at AKU. According to Subhani, with the help of a smart phone application, medical errors in the emergency room could be reduced.

Shaheen Asif, a Master of Science in Nursing student at the School of Nursing and Midwifery, ignited a number of queries when she opined that listening to meditative music or hymns could be more soothing to a patient instead of continuously beeping ICU monitors.

The popularity of the Ignite sessions can be gauged by the fact that two senior members of the AKU faculty Dr Murad Moosa Khan, Professor, Department of Psychiatry and Dr Saad Shafqat, Professor and Chair, Department of Neurology also ignited the minds sharing their valuable experiences. While the former spoke about medicine as a character building profession instead of a business-like commodity, the latter came up with a brain retention strategy to cope with the worrisome trend of brain drain from institutes and from Pakistan at large.

‘I feel, I write, therefore I am’ declared Dr Asad Mian, Associate Professor, Departments of Emergency Medicine and Paediatrics and Child Health. A gripping account of narrative medicine and how writing about patients and patient encounters can generate empathy and compassion and thus impact medical education followed.

AKU’s Rakshinda Mujeeb, a research associate and Muhammad Akbar Baig, a year III Resident also showed their mettle. Mujeeb with her advocacy in favour of pharmacy graduates and Baig with his research on elderly abuse were no less captivating.

CCIT hopes to hold more Ignite events in future, with an ever increasing diversity of speakers and topics.

Kanwal Nayani and Rija Binte Rehan, Final year Medical Students, AKU"
